identity.title: A Radial Decrease in Kinetic Temperature Measured with H<SUB>2</SUB>CO in 30 Doradus

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present sub-parsec observations of H$_2$CO in the 30$\;$Doradus region, which contains the massive star cluster R136 that is clearly exerting feedback on its neighboring gas.

evidence.quote: An approximately 60$\;$pc$\times$90pc region of 30$\;$Doradus was observed by ALMA project 2019.1.00843.S between September and December 2019.
The center of the 30Dor-10 cloud (cite: johansson), $\sim$20pc north-east of R136, was observed at much higher resolution by project 2013.1.00346.S

question.value: Does H2CO-derived gas kinetic temperature in 30 Doradus vary with distance from R136, and which heating mechanisms (mechanical, cosmic ray, X-ray, radiative/photoelectric) explain it?

evidence.quote: H$_2$CO provides a direct measure of gas kinetic temperature, and we find a trend of decreasing temperature with projected distance from R136 that may be indicative of gas heating by the stars.
The first, ALMA project 2019.1.00843.S (cite: wong22) covers a wide region at 1.75$''$$\;$(0.4pc) resolution.
The second, primarily from ALMA project 2013.1.00346.S (cite: indebetouw20) covers a small central region
and 2011.0.00471.S (an older project described in (cite: indebetouw13), which covers a somewhat larger part of the 30Dor-10 cloud

evidence.quote: Both datasets include the H$_2$CO transitions listed in Table [1](#tab:transitions), as well as 232$\;$GHz continuum.

analysis_steps.goal: Image H2CO cubes and make moment maps

method.value: tclean imaging of 12m visibilities at 1.75'' x 0.5 km/s; integrated intensity with threshold mask I(3_03-2_02)>30 mJy/beam, binary-dilated by 3 pixels

95–100% of the 7m flux is recovered by the higher resolution image

method.value: astrodendro on 3_03-2_02; boundaries applied to the other two lines

evidence.quote: the H$_2$CO 3$_{03}$-2$_{02}$ emission is segmented into clumps using `astrodendro`, min_value = 3$\sigma$ = 0.3K, min_delta = 2.5$\sigma$ = 0.25K
min_npix = 1$\;$beam area = 14 square pixels

validation.value: Parameters matter little as only two clumps split into substructure

evidence.quote: The parameters matter very little for subsequent analysis since only two of the clumps break into substructure

analysis_steps.goal: Fit non-LTE kinetic temperature per clump

method.value: chi2 over RADEX grids in n, N, TK and filling factor; peak/expectation values of marginalized posteriors

evidence.quote: For each clump of emission, we calculated $\chi^2$ as a function of $H_2$ volume density $n$, H$_2$CO column density $N$, kinetic temperature $T_K$, and beam areal filling factor *ff*.
If fitting a filling factor, it is important to restrict the filling factor to be less than 1.

assumptions.value: Para-H2CO only, so no ortho-to-para ratio needed

evidence.quote: the three observed H$_2$CO lines are all para-H$_2$CO, so physical conditions can be constrained without assuming an ortho-to-para ratio.

fitting.value: Grid chi2; flat log priors on physical variables; flat linear or log prior on filling factor

evidence.quote: Flat priors in log space were used for the physical variables, and either a flat prior in linear or in log space for the filling factor.

validation.value: Marginalization methods (4D to 1D) give consistent TK; compared with simple and LTE conversions (~20% differences)

evidence.quote: All of those methods result in consistent $T_K$ within uncertainties

method.value: Ratio of averaged 3_21 and 3_22 to 3_03 at 0.6'' for pixels >3 sigma, converted with Tang simple prescription

evidence.quote: Temperature was calculated from that ratio using the "simple" prescription of (cite: tang21) at n(H$_2$)=2$\times$10$^5\;$cm$^{-3}$ and N(H$_2$CO)=10$^{13}\;$cm$^{-2}$.

validation.value: Different masking thresholds tested; morphology robust

evidence.quote: the morphology is robust, as are the indications of internal and external heating

analysis_steps.goal: Radial trend and heating mechanism tests

method.value: Linear fit of TK vs projected distance to R136 maximizing Pearson R over distance range; comparison with continuum, nonthermal linewidth, X-ray and cosmic-ray estimates

evidence.quote: The minimum and maximum projected distance were allowed to vary to maximize the significance of the linear fit as quantified by the Pearson’s correlation coefficient $R$.

findings_qualitative.value: No correlation between TK and continuum or nonthermal linewidth; edges of clumps near R136 hotter, consistent with external heating

evidence.quote: Figure [10](#fig:continuum) shows no such correlation, supporting the hypothesis that external heating dominates in this region.

claims.hypothesis: Gas kinetic temperature decreases with distance from R136
claims.experiment: Non-LTE fits of H2CO line ratios for clumps vs projected distance
claims.result: TK decreases from ~60 to ~20 K over 10-30 pc, no trend beyond 30 pc

evidence.quote: we find a trend of decreasing temperature with projected distance from R136 that may be indicative of gas heating by the stars

claims.experiment: Compare TK with nonthermal linewidth and distance

evidence.quote: we do not observe any correlation between T$_{K}$ and line width

claims.hypothesis: Heating is external rather than internal to clumps
claims.experiment: 0.6'' temperature maps and TK vs continuum
claims.result: Higher ratios on edges of clumps near R136; no TK-continuum correlation

evidence.quote: the clouds closer to R136 do show evidence of higher temperature on the outsides, consistent with external heating.

why_this_method.value: H2CO K-ladder ratios are sensitive to kinetic temperature and weakly to density and column

evidence.quote: should be strongly sensitive to the kinetic temperature, and only weakly to the collider volume density and H$_2$CO column density

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: X-ray heating rejected (would raise TK only ≲10K)

evidence.quote: X-ray heating probably does not dominate, and would only raise the temperature to $\lesssim$10K

limitations_admitted.value: Cosmic ray ionization estimate uncertain by order of magnitude; N(H2CO) poorly constrained

evidence.quote: the conversion of $\gamma$-ray flux to ionization rate is uncertain by an order of magnitude
